newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices rise on crop disease fears.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices rise on crop disease fears.

text.p: Indian cotton prices gained on Wednesday on thin supplies and a possible delay in new arrivals due to the likelyhood of a crop disease, dealers said.
"Mill buying was low but prices rose on reports of a disease in northern India which threatens the cotton crop," one dealer said. No other details of the disease were available.

In spot deals Gujarat Kalyan rose by 200 rupees to 13,800/14,000 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while wagad cotton rose by 300/400 to 11,800/12,000 rupees. Bengal-deshi rose by 25 rupees to 875/900 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) for spot while November delivery (new crop) was quoted at 920/925 rupees.
